title: Strategic reservation sizing and burst-policy review after capacity event
creator: Renee Cho
description: Summary: On 2026-03-08 a Dedicated cluster experienced a multi-tenant capacity event resulting in elevated eviction rates and latency regressions for customer workloads. Root causes were: 1) reservation sizing that used a short sampling window and under-allocated for sustained 99th percentile concurrency, 2) a noisy tenant with high KV-cache footprint that caused uneven GPU memory pressure and degraded co-located tenants, and 3) burst token bucket logic that allowed immediate large bursts post-reservation change, amplifying spike load and triggering autoscaler oscillation. This ticket tracks coordinated follow-ups: a deterministic reservation recalculation, noisy-neighbor detection and temporary isolation workflow, burst policy smoothing and limits, plus telemetry and QA rollout plans.
acceptance_criteria: Reservation recalculation implemented and validated against historical traces with no >10% under-provisioning at 99th percentile
Noisy-tenant detection rule firing on synthetic noisy tenant within 5 minutes and creating an isolation ticket with recommended action
Burst policy changes deployed behind feature flag with controlled canary showing reduced eviction rate by >=50% in Canary vs control
New telemetry (per-tenant GPU mem, sustained concurrency, burst-refill events) ingested and visible on Console dashboards
Playbook updated and assigned; SRE runbook validated in a tabletop run
steps: Instrument and backfill telemetry: per-tenant GPU mem usage, KV-cache miss/hit by tenant, token-bucket events. (owner: Diego Morales, due: 2026-03-17)

Implement reservation formula change: use rolling 1h window with 99th percentile sustained concurrency and a headroom factor per model class. Include opt-out per tenant for manual reservations. (owner: Marcus Kline, due: 2026-03-24)

Add noisy-tenant heuristic: correlated high sustained GPU memory ratio + persistent queueing latency >2x baseline for >5m => mark tenant as noisy. Wire to temporary isolation workflow that moves tenant to isolated cgroup / reserve or throttles admission. (owner: Priya Narang, due: 2026-03-20)

Revise burst policy: change token refill to gradual ramp (linear over 30s) and cap absolute burst tokens per reservation tier. Expose new knobs in Dedicated API and Console. (owner: Liam O'Connor, due: 2026-03-22)
Run offline replay tests using the March-08 trace with baseline and proposed changes; measure evictions, tail latency, and throughput. (owner: Marcus Kline, due: 2026-03-26)
Canary rollout: enable feature-flag in two non-critical clusters, monitor 72h, then promote. (owner: Renee Cho, due: 2026-03-29)
Update playbooks and on-call runbook; schedule tabletop exercise for SRE/Platform (owner: Aisha Patel, due: 2026-03-31)

notes: Observations from replay: short sampling windows (5m) consistently under-sized reservations for tenants with periodic heavy inference pipelines that run every 10-30m. Recommendation: change default window to 1h with configurable tail factor.
Isolation strategy should favor soft-cgroup weights and temporary reservation uplift rather than immediate eviction when possible to avoid customer-visible errors.
Burst policy should be conservative for low-tier reservations; high-tier customers can opt-in to aggressive burst profiles.
We must validate autoscaler hysteresis: current up/down thresholds were symmetric and caused oscillation during spike events. Introduce asymmetric thresholds and cooldowns tied to burst events.
